conflicts.label: Iran 2026 (Day 71)
conflicts.note: Operation Epic Fury — Day 71 (May 9, Saturday — markets closed). NO new US/Israeli strikes on Iran; phase remains blockade + selective F/A-18 disablements + diplomacy. PROJECT FREEDOM paused; restart cleared after Saudi Arabia and Kuwait LIFTED restrictions on US base/airspace access May 7–8 (WSJ, Türkiye Today, The Defense News) following a second Trump–MBS phone call; WSJ: Pentagon could resume operation 'as early as this week' — restart watch is leading scenario edge for Day 72–73. IRAN MoU REPLY SLIPPED past 48-hr Pakistan-channel window; FM Baqaei: 'still reviewing'; Daily Pakistan: talks could resume next week in Islamabad on 14-pt one-month framework MoU. Rubio + Witkoff met Qatari PM Al-Thani in Miami on path to one-page MoU (Axios); Qatar, Pakistan, Egypt, Turkey, Saudi Arabia 'working in tandem.' Pezeshkian publicly conditioned Hormuz negotiations on prior US blockade lifting after disclosed 2.5-hr meeting with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. MAY 8 IRGC seized M/T Ocean Koi in Gulf of Oman under PGSA framework; Iran claims 1 killed / 10 wounded / 5 missing on cargo vessel from May 7–8 US strikes (CENTCOM has not confirmed casualty figures). UAE MoD officially attributed May 8 salvo (flag flipped DISPUTED → UAE-ATTRIBUTED); cumulative UAE intercepts since war start now 551 BMs + 29 CMs. ISRAEL killed at least 24 in Lebanon Saturday — widest strike radius since Apr 17 ceasefire; Saksakieh strike alone killed 7 (incl. 1 child) + 15 wounded; triple-tap drone strike in Nabatieh killed Syrian father and his 12-year-old daughter. Hezbollah retaliated — 1 IDF reservist severely wounded, 2 moderately. Euronews May 10 retrospective puts Saturday south-Lebanon toll at 39. Lebanese MoPH cumulative since Mar 2: 2,783 killed / 8,527 wounded. KHARG ISLAND oil slick 'much reduced' on May 9 Copernicus imagery vs May 6 ~44 sq km peak; Iran officially denies leak (MP Pourkabgani, parliament energy commission head Ahmadi). MARKETS — WEEKEND CARRY: Brent $101.53 / WTI $95.68 (ICE/NYMEX closed Sat); S&P 500 record close 7,398.93 held (Friday +0.84% on April NFP +177k beat); 6-week win streak (longest since 2024); AAA $4.530/gal (−1.6¢ d/d, SECOND consecutive daily decline; +51.5% vs $2.99 Feb 28 baseline). WSJ: Israel ran secret airbase in Iraqi western desert during air campaign — struck Iraqi forces who came close to discovering it (originally attributed to US). USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78) in Atlantic westbound — Day 316 deployed (post-Vietnam record; trailing only Coral Sea 329 / Midway 332); ETA Norfolk mid-to-late May; will enter extended maintenance. USS Boxer ARG eastbound, est. arrival CENTCOM week of May 11. U.S. KIA 15 (carry-forward); WIA 415; cumulative cost midpoint $59.4B (range Pentagon $25.4B → CBS leaked $50.7B → Popular Info $85.2B; spread $59.8B = record). Day 71 places this conflict 28 days past Desert Storm (43 days), 7 days short of Allied Force / Kosovo (78 days), and 5.92× longer than the June 2025 Iran-Israel war (12 days).

conflicts.label: Iraq 2003 (43-day major combat phase)
conflicts.note: Operation Iraqi Freedom — major combat phase (Mar 19 – May 1, 2003, ~43 days). Targets ~19,948 munitions / ~41,000 sorties. US KIA 139 in major combat phase (full OIF 2003-2011 KIA: ~4,431). Cost figure reflects major-combat phase only (~$25B nominal, inflation-adjusted to 2026 $). Full-conflict cumulative (2003-2011) is materially larger at ~$815B nominal / >$1.3T 2026 dollars.

conflicts.label: Libya 2011 (222-day Unified Protector)
conflicts.note: Operation Odyssey Dawn → Unified Protector — NATO no-fly zone (Mar 19 – Oct 31, 2011 = 222 days). NATO total ~26,500 sorties; US strike contribution ~700–1,000 targets (limited US role after handover to NATO Mar 31). US KIA: 0. US cost: ~$1.1B nominal / ~$1.5B 2026 dollars over 222 days = ~$7M/day average.

conflicts.label: Gulf 1991 (43-day Desert Storm air campaign)
conflicts.note: Operation Desert Storm — 38-day air campaign (Jan 17 – Feb 23, 1991) + 100-hour ground war (Feb 24 – Feb 28). ~118,000 coalition sorties, ~38,000+ targets engaged. US KIA: 148 hostile + ~235 non-hostile = ~383 total US deaths during operation. Cost: $61.1B nominal (CRS RL33110); inflation-adjusted to ~$135B in 2026 dollars over 43 days = ~$3.1B/day. 700,000 coalition troops deployed.

conflicts.label: Kosovo 1999 (78-day Allied Force)
conflicts.note: Operation Allied Force — NATO air campaign over Yugoslavia (Mar 24 – Jun 10, 1999 = 78 days). ~38,000 sorties. US KIA: 2 (Apache helicopter crash, training accident in Albania). Cost: ~$3B nominal / ~$5.6B 2026 dollars over 78 days = ~$72M/day average. NATO no-fly zone enforcement + strikes on Yugoslav targets to halt Kosovo operations.

sources: Comparison conflicts use FULL-CONFLICT TOTALS (not Day-21 snapshots). Sources: CRS R44116 (Iraq), RL33110 (Gulf War), R41725 (Libya), RL30374 (Kosovo). Costs inflation-adjusted to 2026 dollars using BLS CPI-U. APPROXIMATIONS: Sortie-counts vs. distinct-target-counts are not always cleanly separable in DoD records; figures cited are best-available open-source estimates and should be read as orders of magnitude. Iraq 2003 cost row reflects ~43-day major combat phase only — full OIF 2003-2011 totals are materially higher (~$815B nominal). Libya 2011 'targets_struck' reflects US strike contribution only (NATO total sorties ~26,500). Iran 2026 row is current state at Day 70 (in progress) and will be updated daily until ceasefire is formalized.
